evidence: The hunk shows _timestamped(audio, aligned) emitting no fidelity while convert_with_timestamps sets x-elvenspeak-alignment, so the streaming path really dropped the signal. The agent's plan also proposed a worst-fidelity header but dropped it because a header must be sent before any sentence is aligned, which is a sound deviation.
guidance_note: When a fix moves a contract to a new carrier (per-object field instead of header), grep every doc and docstring that names the old carrier in the same commit and pin the absence with a test; F47, F48 and F54 were exactly that sweep.

evidence: Four Query(default="mp3_44100_128") literals duplicated formats.DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT; the later F73 hunk shows Query(default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT), so the fix landed.
guidance_note: Before writing a literal default in an endpoint signature, search the module that owns the concept for an exported constant.

evidence: The fixture text starts with a letter and ends inside the last word's phoneme run, so neither gap branch ran; 36a4401 adds leading and trailing gap tests. F49 later showed the trailing test reused DURATIONS and so never exercised real trailing time.
guidance_note: A branch test must vary the input that drives the branch (trailing duration), not just the text; check that the new test fails against a deliberately broken branch.

evidence: elapsed advanced by len(pcm)/2/rate while align used sum(durations); two independent answers to chunk length. But switching to aligned.ends[-1] relied on align() guaranteeing ends[-1]==total, which it did not (F46/F49), and added a dead guard (F89).
guidance_note: When a fix makes one value the source of truth for another, verify the invariant it now relies on (ends[-1] == total + offset) holds on every branch of the producer before switching the consumer.

evidence: The reviewer itself asked to confirm whether Piper ever yields audio without phoneme_alignments, and nothing in the packet settles it. Recording the samples as an unattributed span with measured=False is cheap and loud either way, but it created the trailing-time case F49 found and the doc and test gaps in F65 and F69.
guidance_note: When adding a new state to a producer (unattributed span, measured=False), trace every consumer of that state and the docs that describe its outputs in the same commit, and add a test that constructs it.

evidence: The table has 28 entries; the 36a4401 diff replaces 'thirty' at lines 4, 19, 29, 30, 61 but leaves 'Thirty formats across six codec families' at line 25, which F56/F57/F60 then flagged.
guidance_note: When correcting a repeated factual claim, grep case-insensitively for every spelling (thirty, Thirty, 30) and delete the redundant restatements rather than repainting each.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 on the same line; fixed by the same change to DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT.
b''.join(speech.stream_pcm(...)) ran synchronously inside async def convert, contradicting speech.py's own docstring; the F73 hunk shows it moved to asyncio.to_thread.
guidance_note: When a module docstring claims a property ('synthesis runs off the event loop'), check every call site of that module against it before shipping, not only the path the claim was written for.

evidence: The hunk shows produce() blocking on run_coroutine_threadsafe(queue.put(chunk)).result() against a bounded queue nobody drains after cancellation, and feeder.cancel() is never awaited. The rewrite removed the queue entirely.
guidance_note: For any producer/consumer bridge across threads, write down what happens to each side on consumer abort before shipping, and test the abort path.

evidence: produce()'s finally always pushed the None sentinel, so a mid-synthesis exception looked like clean EOF and ffmpeg exited 0 on truncated audio. A truncated 200 with no error is a direct silent failure.
guidance_note: A sentinel pushed in a finally must carry how the producer ended; never let one end-of-stream value stand for both success and failure.

evidence: Reading stderr only after stdout EOF is a real deadlock pattern, though the reviewer itself notes it is unlikely under -loglevel error. The concurrent stderr task the fix added left 'await errors' with no timeout, which F50 then found.
guidance_note: When adding a concurrent reader task, give every await in the cleanup path the same deadline as the process wait it precedes.

evidence: The hunk shows COPY piper_server/ while the package is elvenspeak/, so docker build fails. The agent admitted its own grep verification excluded the Dockerfile, and added tests/test_dockerfile.py that resolves every COPY source.
guidance_note: After renaming a package, verify with a check that does not share the rename's assumptions (build the image, or parse every file that names paths) rather than an include-filtered grep.

evidence: Same root cause as F9: after BrokenPipeError nothing drains the bounded queue, so the executor thread blocks forever. Resolved by the same queue removal.
The hunk strips PIPER_VOICES entries but compares the raw PIPER_FALLBACK_VOICE; the F66 hunk shows fallback.strip() added.
guidance_note: When a parser normalizes one input, normalize every input compared against it in the same expression.

evidence: int(port_text) accepts -1 and 99999; F98's hunk shows the 1..65535 range check joined to the problems list.
guidance_note: Parsing a config value to a type is not validating its domain; write the range check alongside the parse.

evidence: 'or [text]' always returns a one-element list, so empty text reached synthesize_timed. The fix used min_length=1, which still let whitespace-only text through (F51) despite a new docstring claiming the edge refuses it.
guidance_note: When refusing 'empty' input, define empty the way the downstream parser does (after strip) and test whitespace-only alongside the empty string.

evidence: cat.model() called PiperVoice.load synchronously in async handlers. The agent took the reviewer's second option (pre-load in lifespan) but left Catalog's docstring describing lazy first-request loading, which F94 flagged.
guidance_note: When moving work from lazy to eager, rewrite the docstring of the class that described the lazy behaviour in the same commit.

evidence: Every speak() call passed path='/stream'; 36a4401 adds test_non_streaming_endpoint_returns_encoded_audio.
guidance_note: Before shipping an endpoint table, check each listed endpoint has at least one test that calls it.

evidence: No test hit the settings endpoints; 36a4401 adds shape and 404 tests.
guidance_note: Before shipping an endpoint table, check each listed endpoint has at least one test that calls it.

evidence: SpeechRequest used pydantic's default extra='ignore', so unknown fields were dropped against rule 2. extra='allow' plus model_extra was right for a compatibility server, but the fix skipped the nested VoiceSettings (F68) and made header values caller-controlled (F67's body-field half, F90).
guidance_note: When fixing a rule-2 gap on one model, apply it to every nested model in the same request schema, and treat newly caller-controlled strings as untrusted wherever they are emitted.

evidence: The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted: text became Field(min_length=1, max_length=5000). With auth off by default, unbounded text did reach CPU-bound synthesis. The caller-visible cap went undocumented in the README (F71).
guidance_note: When adding a caller-visible limit, document it where the README lists request rules in the same commit.

evidence: _flag returned False for any unrecognized value, so 'tru' meant off with no report; 36a4401 tests show explicit true/false sets and typos as ConfigError.
guidance_note: Boolean env parsing should have an explicit false-set too, so anything outside both sets is reported.

evidence: Same defect as F10, seen from encode_stream: feeder.cancel() without await loses the exception. F50's hunk shows the rewrite awaits the pump and re-raises its failure as SynthesisFailed.
build() called Settings.from_env() with no ConfigError handling while __main__ did. The shared _settings() helper fixed it but shipped without a test (F82).
guidance_note: A fix whose whole point is a behavioural guarantee (both entry points fail the same way) ships with the test that asserts it.

evidence: Duplicate of F12 (COPY piper_server/ when the package is elvenspeak/), fixed by the same commit.

The model-independent PCM-rate test sat under test_api.py's module-level skipif; 36a4401 moves it to tests/test_encoding.py with no gate. Adding test files made the README's 'format and alignment tests run anywhere' sentence stale (F55).
guidance_note: When adding or moving test modules, update any README prose that enumerates which tests need what.

evidence: The build script split PIPER_VOICES without stripping, unlike Settings.from_env. The fix copied the strip rule into the Dockerfile with a comment asserting the two agree (shown in F77's hunk), which F77 then flagged as a duplicate implementation.
guidance_note: When two code paths disagree about parsing the same input, make one call the other (Settings.from_env) instead of copying the rule; a comment saying 'stripped exactly as X' is a sign the duplication survived.

evidence: HEALTHCHECK hardcoded 127.0.0.1:5001 while PORT is overridable. The fix left EXPOSE 5001 beside it (F70) and added no regression test (F78).
guidance_note: When removing one hardcoded copy of a value, grep the file for every other literal of that value (EXPOSE 5001) and pin the fix with a test.

evidence: COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest is unpinned; the F76 hunk shows uv:0.9.10 and 36a4401 adds a no-:latest test.
guidance_note: Pin every external image tag at the moment it is written.

evidence: Third report of the F12 COPY defect; fixed by the same commit.
Duplicate of F29; uv pinned to 0.9.10.
Duplicate of F6. The reply claims 'all eight occurrences corrected', but 36a4401 left 'Thirty formats' at formats.py:25, so the claim was false and three round-1 threads re-raised it.
guidance_note: Before replying 'all N occurrences corrected', rerun the grep on the committed tree and quote its empty output.

evidence: This finding names all three blocking call sites. Later hunks (F46, F84) show synthesize_timed wrapped in asyncio.to_thread in both timestamp endpoints too, so the sweep was complete even though the reply mentions only the non-streaming handler.
Third duplicate of F2; fixed together.

The duplication is real, but the hunk opens with <!-- BEGIN LIT INTEGRATION -->, the marker of a block lit init regenerates. A hand edit or sync comment would be silently overwritten, so declining here and pointing the fix at the upstream template is correct.

Starlette commits the 200 before pulling from the generator, so the docstring's '500 rather than an empty 200' was false for streaming. The F97 hunk shows the corrected docstring scoping the 500 to non-streaming endpoints.
guidance_note: A docstring that promises an error-handling outcome must name which code paths deliver it; check streaming paths separately.

evidence: Resolution logic was tested only under the model-gated test_api.py. The new tests/test_voices.py in 36a4401 asserts against the live aliases.toml contents (Rachel to hfc_female), which F64 flagged, and bypasses install() so a bad fallback was constructible (F63).
guidance_note: Unit tests for a pure function should feed it fixture data, not the shipped data file; if the function can't take the data as a parameter, that is the design defect to fix first.

evidence: aliases.toml was parsed lazily via cached_property, so a malformed edit surfaced as a 500. Touching the cached property in install() made it eager; F64's fix later replaced that private poke with load_aliases().
guidance_note: Prefer loading external data at the boundary and passing it in over forcing a lazy property from outside.

evidence: The text is the lit-integration block between generated markers, an operator-authored instruction for one read-only command; calling it a prompt-injection pattern overstates it. Declining to hand-edit a regenerated block is correct, though the 'will be reverted' reasoning was the weaker argument (F88 said so).
No USER instruction; the F70 hunk shows useradd plus USER elvenspeak, and 36a4401 tests for a USER line.
guidance_note: Container templates should include a non-root USER from the first draft.

evidence: _aliases filters to installed voices and no alias targets en_US-lessac-medium, so the default config made the table inert. The README fix gave a PIPER_VOICES example with only 4 of the 9 targets (36a4401 README diff), which F53 flagged.
guidance_note: When documenting a command that should 'make them live', derive it from the data file (all nine targets) instead of typing a sample.

evidence: install() checked only the .onnx before skipping download, while _describe opens the .onnx.json. The fix checks both before downloading but not after, which F72 found.
guidance_note: When adding a completeness check before an operation that is supposed to produce the state, run the same check after it too.

evidence: from_env had no tests; 36a4401 adds tests/test_settings.py covering each branch and the multi-problem report.
guidance_note: A pure parser over dict[str,str] should ship with its branch tests in the PR that adds it.

evidence: The hunk splices '${PIPER_VOICES}' into a Python literal inside a shell RUN, so a single quote escapes into code at build time. The fix reads os.environ, pinned by test_the_build_arg_is_not_spliced_into_source_text.
guidance_note: Never interpolate a build arg into source text; pass it through the environment from the first draft.

evidence: /health returned metadata from _describe and never loaded a model, so 'exercises a real synthesis path' was false. With F17's eager loading the corrected weaker claim is accurate.
guidance_note: Comments describing what a healthcheck proves should be checked against the handler it calls.

evidence: F4's fix set elapsed = aligned.ends[-1] (hunk line 3419), but align() never extended ends[-1] to total when no trailing character existed. The previous len(pcm) offset did not under-count, so the fix introduced drift; 667428e's test fails on the old code by 0.2s per sentence.
guidance_note: Before switching a consumer to read a producer's field as 'the total', assert in a test that the field equals the total on every producer branch.

evidence: F1's fix deliberately omitted x-elvenspeak-alignment on the streaming endpoint without pinning the omission. A real but small gap: the absence is client-observable, so the one-line assertion is cheap and justified.
guidance_note: When a fix's design decision is an absence (no header), assert the absence in the same test that checks the new carrier.

evidence: alignment.py's module docstring (hunk line 3532) still said the endpoints report fidelity in a header after F1's fix moved streaming to per-object alignment_fidelity. Deleting the clause about another module's behaviour is a better fix than qualifying it.
guidance_note: When changing how a value is transported, grep for the old carrier's name (x-elvenspeak-alignment) across code docstrings and README in the same commit.

evidence: F5's fix appends a synthetic ' ' phoneme with real duration for unattributed audio, so total includes time no character receives; the 'if char_cursor < len(characters)' gate (hunk line 3597) drops it. Combined with F4's ends[-1] offset this drifts the stream. F3's trailing test reused DURATIONS and missed it.
guidance_note: When a fix makes durations sum to the audio, also assert the alignment's last end equals that sum, so the invariant is enforced where it is consumed.

evidence: The ad22896 rewrite for F11 added errors = create_task(process.stderr.read()) and an unbounded 'stderr = await errors' (hunk line 3663) before the timed process.wait(). On an aborted stream a wedged ffmpeg never closes stderr, so cleanup hangs before reaching the kill. The original code killed first and so could not hang here.
guidance_note: When rewriting subprocess cleanup, order it so the bounded kill path is reachable from every await, and put each await under the same deadline.

evidence: F16/F21's fix used min_length=1 (hunk line 3719), which admits '   ', while split_sentences' new docstring claimed the edge refuses empty text; whitespace-only got a 200 with an empty body. parse-dont-validate fits the validator; no-mode-explosion is pasted onto a preference about str_strip_whitespace.
guidance_note: When refusing empty input at the edge, define empty with the same normalization (strip) the downstream code applies and test whitespace-only.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: FROM python:3.12-slim is unchanged from the round-0 Dockerfile (F12 hunk), so the finding is pre-existing. The drift is real, though requires-python '>=3.12' is a floor rather than a copy; a test tying them is a cheap answer.
guidance_note: When a Dockerfile names a language version, add the test tying it to .python-version in the first draft.

evidence: The 36a4401 README diff adds a PIPER_VOICES example with 5 voices (4 alias targets) under 'To make them live'; 973bad3 replaces it with all nine targets.
guidance_note: When documenting a command that should 'make them live', derive it from the data file (all nine targets) instead of typing a sample.

evidence: The README still said fidelity 'is reported: x-elvenspeak-alignment' unconditionally after F1's fix stopped sending it on /stream/with-timestamps; 973bad3's README diff names both carriers.
guidance_note: When changing how a value is transported, grep for the old carrier's name across docs in the same commit.

evidence: Round-0 fixes (F26, F37, F43) added test_encoding/test_settings/test_voices/test_dockerfile, making 'The format and alignment tests run anywhere' an incomplete enumeration; 973bad3 restates it as the single exception.
guidance_note: When adding test modules, update any README prose that enumerates which tests need what.

evidence: 36a4401 changed 'thirty' at lines 4, 19, 29, 30 and 61 but left 'Thirty formats across six codec families' at line 25 (hunk line 3984); 973bad3 deletes the redundant count.
guidance_note: When correcting a repeated factual claim, grep case-insensitively for every spelling and delete the restatements rather than repainting each.

evidence: Same missed 'Thirty' at formats.py:25 as F56; one deletion in 973bad3 resolved all three threads.

The F10/F23 fix (ad22896) made a mid-synthesis failure raise SynthesisFailed, but no test fed a raising generator; tests/test_encoding.py only uses clean buffers. 0623b57 adds yield-then-raise and raise-before-yield tests.
guidance_note: A fix for a silent-failure bug ships with a test that injects the failure and asserts the error surfaces.

evidence: install() had no tests at all, including the eager alias parse F38's fix added and the both-halves check from F42. The reviewer names 'this very round's own fix' as untested; e78b8d1 adds tests/test_install.py.
guidance_note: A fix whose purpose is 'fail at boot instead of at request' ships with a test that drives the boot function into that failure.

evidence: Third thread on the same missed 'Thirty' at formats.py:25; resolved by the 973bad3 deletion.

Flag is a false positive: the 'MP3 offers 32 kbps only at 22.05 kHz' sentence is in the original _build_formats docstring and 36a4401 did not touch it. The table includes (44100, 32), so the example was false; 973bad3 deletes it.
guidance_note: Illustrative examples in a docstring next to a table should be checked against that table before shipping, or left out.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: resolve()'s 'Only the third is a substitution' docstring is original code. It contradicts the alias branch's substituted=True, which test_alias_resolves_when_its_target_is_installed asserts; 973bad3 deletes the clause.

Flag is a false positive: Catalog.__init__ accepting any fallback is original code, only made visible by F37's test helper. Moving the check into __init__ and deleting install()'s copy, rather than adding a second check, is the single-enforcer answer.
guidance_note: Put a class's invariants in its constructor from the start, so test helpers that build it directly cannot build an invalid one.

evidence: F37's new tests/test_voices.py asserts '21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM' maps to hfc_female, reading the live aliases.toml through the module-level _ALIASES_FILE. The agent confirmed that injecting the table immediately broke two tests that had been reading the live file.
guidance_note: Unit tests for a pure function should feed it fixture data, not the shipped data file; if the function can't take the data as a parameter, fix that first.

evidence: F5's fix added a second INTERPOLATED trigger (measured=False) that the README did not mention, and 'spread evenly' misdescribed it. 973bad3's README diff names both triggers.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new cause for an output flag, update the user-facing description of that flag in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 'elif fallback is not None and voices and fallback not in voices' is in the round-0 hunk (line 1873); F14's fix only added the strip above it. The guard did suppress the second problem when PIPER_VOICES was empty.
guidance_note: In an accumulate-all-problems validator, don't gate one check on another field's validity unless the check can't be evaluated.

evidence: Flag is mostly a false positive: the voice_id-into-header path is in the round-0 headers() code. Only the body-field half became reachable through F20's extra='allow'. The agent confirmed the old code raised UnicodeEncodeError. The backslashreplace fix only escaped non-ASCII and let CR/LF through (F79).
guidance_note: When escaping caller text for a header, define the allowed set positively (printable ASCII minus the escape and separator characters) instead of escaping only what fails an encode.

evidence: F20's fix put extra='allow' on SpeechRequest only; VoiceSettings (hunk line 4668) kept the default, so unknown voice_settings fields were still dropped.
guidance_note: When fixing a rule-2 gap on one model, apply it to every nested model in the same request schema.

evidence: F5's fix added the 'elif samples:' unattributed-span branch (hunk line 4724) with no test constructing such a chunk; only align() was tested with measured=False handed in. 0623b57 adds a duck-typed fake.
guidance_note: A fix for a silent-failure bug ships with a test that constructs the triggering input at the producer, not just at the consumer.

evidence: EXPOSE 5001 sat beside the HEALTHCHECK F28 fixed. The reviewer's -P runtime scenario cannot be solved by EXPOSE (build-time), which the agent stated; EXPOSE ${PORT} only removes the build-time duplicate. The reply-hint 'already_fixed' is wrong; the agent changed code in c26a90e.
guidance_note: When removing one hardcoded copy of a value, grep the file for every other literal of it.

evidence: F21's fix added MAX_TEXT_LENGTH=5000, a caller-visible 422, with no README mention; the d32a9c8 README diff documents it under rule 3.
guidance_note: When adding a caller-visible limit, document it where the README lists request rules in the same commit.

evidence: F42's fix checks both files before download_voice (hunk line 4888) but goes straight to _describe after it, so a half-written download crashes there. The test suite also never entered the download branch.
guidance_note: When adding a completeness check before an operation that is supposed to produce the state, run the same check after it too.

evidence: F8/F33's to_thread fix newly allowed concurrent synthesize() on one cached PiperVoice. The agent cites piper/voice.py:24 _ESPEAK_PHONEMIZER_LOCK and ONNX concurrent Run(), and d32a9c8 adds a 4-thread test, but the piper source is not in the packet and a passing 4-way run is weak race evidence.
guidance_note: When moving shared-object calls onto worker threads, check and record the library's thread-safety in the same commit, with the concurrency test, before a reviewer asks.

evidence: The hunk shows __init__ validating fallback (F63's fix) beside the new aliases parameter (F64's fix) with no check, while resolve() indexes _voices[aliased]. The agent concedes 'I closed this exact hole for fallback and left the parameter I had just added open beside it'.
guidance_note: When adding a constructor parameter in the same round as a constructor invariant, apply the invariant to every parameter resolve() indexes with.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 'process.returncode not in (0, -9)' is byte-identical to the round-0 code (F10 hunk line 1596). An external SIGKILL closes stdout, the loop sees EOF, and -9 passed as success; killed_here makes the exemption depend on what this function did.
guidance_note: Don't infer 'we did this' from an exit code; record it in a local where the action happens.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the missing .dockerignore dates from the original Dockerfile; no fix created it. .venv/ and models/ are gitignored and would ship as build context.
guidance_note: Add .dockerignore, derived from .gitignore, in the same commit as a Dockerfile.

evidence: F27/F44's fix produced '[download_voice(v.strip(), d) for v in os.environ[...].split(',') if v.strip()]' under a comment saying entries are stripped 'exactly as Settings.from_env strips them' (hunk lines 5193-5199), a second implementation of the same parse.
guidance_note: When two code paths disagree about parsing the same input, make one call the other instead of copying the rule; a comment asserting they agree means the duplication survived.

evidence: F28's HEALTHCHECK fix and F70's EXPOSE ${PORT} fix shipped with no assertion in tests/test_dockerfile.py, which already parses the Dockerfile for this kind of check.
guidance_note: When a test file already exists for a file's invariants, add the new invariant to it in the same commit as the fix.

evidence: F67's _ascii_safe used encode('ascii','backslashreplace') (hunk line 5315), which passes CR/LF. The agent confirmed the raw CRLF arrived intact in x-elvenspeak-voice-requested, and d32a9c8's tests send %0D%0A and check every C0 codepoint.
guidance_note: When escaping caller text for a header, define the allowed set positively (printable ASCII) and test every control codepoint, not just the non-ASCII example that prompted the fix.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: _describe's config.get('language', {}).get('code') is original code that no review fix touched. An explicit null returns None and the chained .get raises AttributeError.
guidance_note: When reading an external JSON file, treat null and absent the same at every lookup in the parser at once.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the key-derived fallback in _describe is original code. It sat untested because make_voice() in F59's test module always wrote complete sidecars.
F24's fix introduced _settings() so both entry points exit 2 with every problem, and shipped no test; d32a9c8 adds tests/test_main.py.
guidance_note: A fix whose whole point is a behavioural guarantee (both entry points fail the same way) ships with the test that asserts it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the 'if cat else []' in /health is in the round-0 hunk (line 1195). Catalog has no __bool__ and app.state raises AttributeError, so the branch is dead.
guidance_note: Don't write a fallback branch without checking that its condition can actually be falsy.

evidence: F67's fix added the comment 'Every response header this service sends is built here', while convert_with_timestamps assigns x-elvenspeak-alignment after headers() returns (hunk line 5607), bypassing _ascii_safe.
guidance_note: Before writing 'every X goes through here', grep for every site that writes X and route them, or narrow the claim.

evidence: F80's fix changed language and audio to '(config.get(...) or {})' but left int(config.get('num_speakers', 1)) two lines below (hunk line 5671); the agent concedes two of three fields were fixed.
guidance_note: When fixing a null-vs-absent bug in one lookup, sweep every .get(key, default) in the same function.

evidence: After F80's fix, quality tolerated a missing or null 'audio' while sample_rate=int(config['audio']['sample_rate']) in the same constructor raised a bare KeyError/TypeError. Correctly made a named failure, not a default.
guidance_note: When fixing a null-vs-absent bug in one lookup, sweep every lookup of the same section in the function, deciding default-or-fail for each.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: ENV PIPER_VOICES=${PIPER_VOICES} is unchanged from the round-0 Dockerfile (F28 hunk line 2554). Whether Docker word-splits a substituted ENV value is not shown anywhere in the packet, and the agent reported Docker would not run on its machine (F12), so neither side verified the premise.
guidance_note: When a Dockerfile claim depends on Docker's parsing semantics, verify with an actual build (or cite the documented behaviour) before both writing and accepting it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: this re-raises F39 against unchanged lit-generated text, not against a fix. The agent concedes the earlier 'will be reverted' argument was weak, gives a better one (operator's own narrow instruction, not untrusted content), and routes the decision to the owner.
guidance_note: When declining a finding, lead with the substantive reason it is wrong rather than a reason about where the fix would live.

evidence: F4's fix wrote 'elapsed = aligned.ends[-1] if aligned.ends else elapsed' (hunk line 5884). split_sentences filters empty pieces, so the else branch is unreachable, and if reached it would silently reuse a stale offset.
guidance_note: Don't add an else-keep-previous guard to a fix without proving the empty case is reachable; if it is, fail loudly instead.

evidence: F20's extra='allow' made ignored names arbitrary JSON keys, so a key containing ', ' became ambiguous after the join. The case is pathological; escaping commas without changing the documented wire format is proportionate, but escaping commas before _ascii_safe created the backslash ambiguity F95 found.
guidance_note: When adding a second escape step to a value that already has one, merge them into one pass with one escape character that is itself escaped.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: ARG PIPER_VOICES=en_US-lessac-medium is unchanged from the round-0 Dockerfile. The drift risk against settings.DEFAULT_VOICE is real but minor; b6bc56f adds the test the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When a Dockerfile ARG repeats a code constant, add the tying test in the first draft.

evidence: F77's fix reused Settings.from_env but kept its own download_voice loop (hunk line 6058), with no post-download completeness check. Calling voices.install() (b6bc56f diff) deletes the second implementation, which is better than the reviewer's add-a-check.
guidance_note: When a review says 'this duplicates X's parsing', check whether the whole step duplicates X's operation and reuse the operation, not just the parser.

evidence: F76's .dockerignore listed .pytest_cache/ and .ruff_cache/ that .gitignore did not; the agent says it wrote the list from scratch instead of starting from .gitignore. The reply-hint 'pushback' is wrong; b6bc56f adds both entries.
guidance_note: Derive a new ignore file from the existing one, then add only what differs.

evidence: F17's fix made the lifespan load every voice, but Catalog's docstring (hunk line 6148) still said the first request for a voice pays for the load and reasoned about racing first requests.
guidance_note: When moving work from lazy to eager, rewrite the docstring of the class that described the lazy behaviour in the same commit.

evidence: F90's fix escaped commas as backslash-x2c before _ascii_safe, which passes literal backslashes, so caller text containing 'backslash-x2c' is indistinguishable from an escaped comma. 7940d45 escapes backslash, comma and non-printables in one pass and tests that the encoding is reversible.
guidance_note: When adding a second escape step to a value that already has one, merge them into one pass with one escape character that is itself escaped.

evidence: F86's fix checked 'if rate is None' (hunk line 6271), letting sample_rate 0 through to a ZeroDivisionError in align()'s _seconds at request time; the agent concedes it is 'the same distinction one value along'.
guidance_note: When writing a boot-time refusal for an unusable value, define unusable by what the consumer divides or indexes with (rate <= 0), not by absence alone.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: Prosody.speaker_id is original code that no review fix touched. The agent confirmed nothing assigns it; deleting it was one of the reviewer's two options and fits the no-invented-body-field constraint.
guidance_note: Don't add a knob without the code path that sets it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the PIPER_MODELS_DIR read (hunk line 6391) is original code. An empty value becomes Path('.') and mkdir succeeds silently; the reply-hint 'pushback' is wrong, since 8fff127 adds the check to the problems list.
guidance_note: In a validate-everything config parser, list every env var it reads and give each a validation rule, including 'present but empty'.

narrative: A 5166-line new service got 98 findings over five reviewed rounds; a sixth round was capped and read nothing. 37 of the 53 findings after round 0 came from earlier fixes, the largest class being missed sibling instances (thirty to 28 at line 25, num_speakers beside language, sample_rate 0 beside null, VoiceSettings beside SpeechRequest). Others were fixes shipped without their regression test (F58, F59, F69, F78, F82) and docs left stale by a fix (F48, F54, F65, F71, F94). Two fixes created real regressions: F4's ends[-1] offset relied on an invariant align() did not keep (F46), and F11's stderr task made cleanup hang (F50). Every round from 1 to 4 also raised findings on untouched original code, so no round was purely avoidable and avoidable_rounds is 0.
guidance_observations: The agent's round-0 reply claimed 'all eight occurrences corrected' for a count fix that missed one, which cost three duplicate threads; a closing grep quoted in the reply would have caught it.
Fixes repeatedly copied a rule instead of calling its owner (Dockerfile strip, then Dockerfile download loop), and each copy drew its own finding before the agent reached for voices.install().

From round 1 on, the agent's habit of deleting redundant restatements instead of repainting them (format counts, docstring claims about other modules, README enumerations) stopped those threads from recurring.

Most round-0 fixes landed without the test that would prove them, and the next round asked for those tests one at a time; writing the failure-injection test with each fix would have removed a class of findings.
Pushbacks were handled well: F35/F39/F88 were declined with an owner escalation, and F73 was declined with verification and a concurrency test rather than an unneeded lock.
